subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should OpenClaw add automatic Feishu group per-sender subAgent lifecycle, and if so should it be a Feishu plugin-owned opt-in feature rather than a core orchestration default?
rationale: The request crosses Feishu routing, agent creation, per-agent skills/config, memory isolation, quotas, cleanup, and security boundaries, so automation cannot choose the product contract safely.

options.title: Design Plugin-Owned Automation First
options.body: Keep the issue open and require a Feishu plugin-owned opt-in design covering routing, authorization, memory namespaces, config writes, quotas, cleanup, and live proof before implementation.

options.title: Constrain To Existing Seams
options.body: Treat groupSessionScope, explicit bindings, and thread-bound sessions as the supported pattern, then split or close the automatic subAgent lifecycle request.

options.title: Split Into Smaller Canonicals
options.body: Break the feature into separate issues for group sender memory isolation, skill preferences, threading ergonomics, and lifecycle/admin controls.

recommendation.title: Design Plugin-Owned Automation First
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and require a Feishu plugin-owned opt-in design covering routing, authorization, memory namespaces, config writes, quotas, cleanup, and live proof before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue is primarily a Feishu plugin behavior decision and the Feishu plugin reference identifies m1heng as the community maintainer.
